policy_title: Establish Great British Energy and Drive Clean Power by 2030
stated: Labour will create Great British Energy, a new publicly-owned company capitalised with £8.3 billion, to co-invest with industry and trade unions in leading clean energy technologies and deploy local energy production. This is part of a mission to achieve cheaper, zero-carbon electricity by 2030, aiming to double onshore wind, triple solar, and quadruple offshore wind, while investing in carbon capture, hydrogen, and marine energy.

source.quote: To deliver our clean power mission, Labour will work with the private sector to double onshore wind, triple solar power, and quadruple offshore wind by 2030. We will invest in carbon capture and storage, hydrogen and marine energy, and ensure we have the long-term energy storage our country needs. Labour will create a new publiclyowned company, Great British Energy. It will be owned by the British people and deliver power back to the British people. Great British Energy will partner with industry and trade unions to deliver clean power by co-investing in leading technologies; will help support capital-intensive projects; and will deploy local energy production to benefit communities across the country. To support this, Labour will capitalise Great British Energy with £8.3 billion, over the next parliament. Labour will deploy more distributed production capacity through our Local Power Plan. Great British Energy will partner with energy companies, local authorities, and co-operatives to install thousands of clean power projects, through a combination of onshore wind, solar, and hydropower projects.

bearing_set.reason: The policy's central purpose is decarbonising electricity generation — directly affecting emissions trajectory, a core O6 indicator.
The policy explicitly targets 'cheaper electricity' for households; energy bills are a direct O2 indicator, and the effect (positive or contested) is non-negligible.

£8.3bn public capitalization plus a large-scale clean energy infrastructure buildout directly affects productivity, business investment, and long-term real living standards — dual-horizon: near-term transition costs vs long-term cheaper/secure energy supply.

£8.3bn capitalization of a publicly-owned company, plus the broader public financing of the 2030 clean-power mission, is a material fiscal commitment that moves the funded/borrowed balance and debt-path indicators, warranting a real verdict regardless of whether GBE generates returns.

membership_note: Four fundamentals bear on this policy: the environmental mission (O6), the stated consumer energy-price goal (O2), the macroeconomic investment/productivity effect (O13), and the fiscal commitment (O12). Labour market effects (O4) are secondary — the trade-union co-investment angle is noted but does not clear the non-negligible bar for a distributional labour-quality verdict on its own.
